subject: Latent marginal predicted values from INLA GLMM?

messages.author: 90a8e1d81ee67e59
messages.subject: Latent marginal predicted values from INLA GLMM?
parts:
Hi all,

I am wondering whether it is possible in INLA to obtain marginal predicted values (computed using only fixed effects) for original data on the latent scale?

A little background to clarify my problem:
I am currently running animal models in R INLA to do variance component analysis. However I would like to get the variance estimates on the data scale rather than the latent model scale (more biologically interesting) and am using a convenient package "QGglmm" to do this (see attached paper and how to PDF). On page 22-23 of the "how to use QGglmm" PDF you will see that, when fixed effects are included in a model, the package requires "yhat": marginal predicted values from the INLA model (computed using only fixed effects), and the predictions must be computed on the latent scale. As comparison, in an MCMCglmm model output the predict(model, type="terms") function would allow me to get these values.

Currently I have used "control.compute=list(dic=T,config = TRUE)" when running my INLA models, and obtained the predicted values for my original data (i.e. not including NAs in the response phenotype) using "Data$summary.fitted.values". Then I transform these values to the latent scale using the link function (logit link for my binary models, log link for my zero inflated negative binomial model).

I am wondering if random effects affect these fitted values ("predictions"), or whether they are computed using only fixed effects. I also wonder if it is correct to use the log link to transform fitted values to the latent model scale for the "zeroinflatednbinomial1" family.

Thanks in advance,

Sarah Lundregan
NTNU Trondheim, Norway

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Latent marginal predicted values from INLA GLMM?
parts:
the predictions from the fitted values are computed from the linear
predictor using like exp(linear.predictor), if the link function is the
'log' (and the appropriate flag is given to do so, link=...)

If the linear predictor contains random effects, then those are
included in the fitted values. Often, is the random effects are of the
'classical style', like model="iid", then their mean is zero so the
predictions with and without the random effects will mostly differ in
the variance (although E(exp(...)) depends also on the variance of
...).

You can easily compute the predictions only using the fixed effect if
you want to, either by using posterior samples, as you mention, or
using linear combinations (see the FAQ page).

If you want to predict the outcome of the zeroinflated output, then its
much easier to stay with the posterior sample stuff. (see also
inla.posterior.sample.eval() which simplify life...)

Best
H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Latent marginal predicted values from INLA GLMM?
parts:
Hi,

That the predictions for the fitted values are computed from the linear predictor, meaning they are influenced by and random effects in the predictor, is as I suspected.

Because mine is an animal model, it includes generic0 random effects e.g. in the form of the A inverse. As these type of effects are not of the classical style then probably I cannot assume a mean of zero, hence these type of random effects may influence the predictions.

I would therefore like to compute the predictions using only the fixed effects by posterior sampling, however have been having a difficult time trying to achieve this over the past weeks. Could you possibly give a brief explanation of how to do this for an example model where x1 and x2 are continuous covariates, x3 is a factor with 3 levels, and f(animal) and f(year) are the two random effects that I do not want to influence the predictions for y:

y ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + f(year, model="iid"...) + f(animal, model="generic0, Cmatrix=Ainv...)

Best,
Sarah
